title: Dedicated reservation bundling, routing, and autoscale templates
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers requesting Dedicated reservations routinely over- or under-provision capacity because the current intake form and approval flow treat every request as an independent cluster. This causes unnecessary fragmentation of GPU pools, unpredictable throughput per tenant, and poor autoscaling behavior.

Goal: Define a provisioning workflow that supports bundling reservation requests into capacity bundles, deterministic routing rules for throughput guarantees, and a small set of autoscaling policy templates that matches common workloads. Deliver a decision record, intake templates, approval guardrails, and a plan for instrumentation to validate capacity forecasts.

Scope: This ticket covers product-facing artifacts (intake template + routing rules + autoscale templates), an approval decision matrix by org tier, and a capacity planning heuristic for the Capacity Planning team. Implementation tasks (API changes, scheduler routing engine) will be tracked as dependent ENG tickets.

Deliverables:
- Reservation bundling model and business rules (how and when requests are aggregated)
- Routing policy definitions to map bundles to physical fleets with throughput guarantees (latency/throughput SLOs)
- Three autoscale policy templates (burst-capable low-latency, cost-optimized steady, and mixed workload) with recommended thresholds and KPIs
- Updated intake form fields and examples for customers to supply traffic profiles and critical windows
- Approval guardrails for Capacity, Sales, and Legal (including required artifacts)
- Measurement plan (dashboards + alerts) to validate forecast vs actual utilization for first 90 days

Why different: Instead of one-off reservations this design introduces capacity bundles (logical pools spanning related requests) and routing rules so fleet controls can provide stronger throughput guarantees while improving utilization.
acceptance_criteria: Product spec reviewed and signed off by Capacity, Sales Engineering, and Legal
Intake template includes traffic profile, 95th percentile tokens/sec estimate, and critical windows
Minimum three autoscale templates documented with example threshold values and billing signal mappings
Approval matrix that maps customer tier + risk profile to required artifacts and signoff steps
Measurement plan with dashboard queries and a 90-day validation window documented
Dependencies to ENG tickets are identified and handoff notes exist in linked Confluence page

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot, 4 weeks): Offer bundling opt-in to three existing enterprise customers. Instrument dashboards and manual approval steps. Phase 2 (gradual rollout, 6 weeks): Auto-bundle requests per business unit and enable routing to pooled fleets for new reservations. Phase 3: Enforce bundling as default and add UI in Console for customers to join/leave bundles. Communicate changes via Customer Success playbook and Release Notes.
sample_intake_template: Requested capacity: GPU count and instance type; Traffic profile: 95th percentile tokens/sec, average req/sec, peak windows (ISO dates); SLA target: 95% requests < X ms; Desired start/end dates; Business unit and app tag; Flexibility: burstable / fixed throughput; Billing model: committed / burstable overage; Compliance flags: data residency, SOC2 / HIPAA; Attachments: 3-month traffic sample (CSV) and target backlog PRD.
autoscale_templates_summary: 1) Latency-first burst (recommended for low-latency customer-facing APIs): min_replicas=2, burst_max=4, scale_up_threshold=70% token-concurrency, cooldown=30s. 2) Cost-optimized steady (recommended for batch/embeddings workloads): min_replicas=1, max_replicas=8, scale_up_threshold=85% sustained for 5m, cooldown=5m. 3) Mixed workload (recommended for mixed chat + embeddings): min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12, hot-path reserve=1 replica, token-based autoscaling metric with predictive headroom of 20%.
routing_policy_examples: - Preferred routing: Assign bundles to fleets in same region and capacity tier; prefer lower-latency nodes when SLO is <100ms. - Fallback routing: If preferred fleet is exhausted, route to compatible model variant with soft SLO (increase latency budget) and notify CS. - Emergency throttle: For sudden overload, limit per-tenant qps to pre-agreed throughput until autoscale catches up.
capacity_planning_heuristic: Heuristic to convert request profiles into reservation units: (95th_tokens_sec * expected_concurrent_users) / per-GPU_throughput = required_GPUs. Add 25% headroom for burstable SLAs or 10% for committed throughput. Aggregate requests into bundles when start dates within 30 days and business unit overlap >50%.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-bundling could create noisy-neighbor issues — mitigation: soft isolation via hot-path reserves and per-tenant qps caps. Risk: Sales may promise throughput guarantees that aren’t backed by fleet capacity — mitigation: approval guardrails that require Capacity signoff for P0 throughput guarantees.
